name: Naturalisation as a Dutch National

requirements.blocker_text: Must have lived in the Kingdom of the Netherlands (which includes Curacao) for at least 5 consecutive years with a valid residence permit; exceptions to this timeframe exist but were not detailed in the source reviewed.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 consecutive years of lawful residence with a valid residence permit within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

requirements.blocker_text: Must have passed the civic integration exam at Dutch language level A2 or above; exemptions apply if sufficient Dutch proficiency (reading, writing, speaking, comprehension) is otherwise demonstrated.
requirements.fix_path: Pass the civic integration exam at A2 level or demonstrate equivalent Dutch proficiency.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicant must be at least 18 years old.
Must not be a danger to public order or national security of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
Must generally renounce current nationality, with limited exemptions.

evidence_required.document: Civic integration exam certificate (A2+) or proof of exemption
Proof of 5 years' valid residence permit history
Attendance at the mandatory naturalisation ceremony (within 1 year of approval) and Declaration of Solidarity
Fees (amount not specified in the pages reviewed; see IND's separate fees page)

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 5 consecutive years, continuously, with a valid residence permit

sources.title: Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst (IND), Kingdom of the Netherlands -- Becoming a Dutch national through naturalisation: 5-year residence requirement, A2 civic integration exam, age 18+, public order requirement, renunciation of prior nationality, naturalisation ceremony

IND -- Becoming a Dutch national in the Caribbean part of the Kingdom: naturalisation and option procedures, naturalisation ceremony and Declaration of Solidarity requirement, fees payable via the Curacao Admission Office (Immigratiedienst Curacao)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Curacao's initial build. Naturalisation for Curacao residents is administered under Kingdom-wide Dutch nationality law by the IND, not by a separate Curacao citizenship regime -- the Curacao Admission Office (Immigratiedienst Curacao) handles the local application/fee-collection step (fee confirmed there as XCG 615, not repeated here since it is a Kingdom-level, not Curacao-specific, figure). dual_citizenship_allowed is set to false based on the general renunciation requirement stated on the naturalisation page, though the same page notes 'limited exemptions' exist without detailing them -- treat this as the general rule, not an absolute one. An 'option procedure' (a faster, narrower route for specific grounds -- born in the Kingdom, recognised by a Dutch parent, long-term Kingdom residence, born before 1985 to a Dutch mother, or former Dutch nationals) also exists and is NOT modelled as this route; see cw_option_long_residence.json for the one option ground plausible for a migrant to actively pursue, modelled separately and in draft due to an unconfirmed duration figure. Notably, the IND option-procedure page as fetched in this pass did not list marriage/partnership to a Dutch national as its own option ground, which is somewhat surprising relative to general knowledge of Dutch nationality law -- flagged rather than assumed to be an omission in the source.
